newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MANEY SINKS AS LIQUIDITY SHARTAGE FADES.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MANEY SINKS AS LIQUIDITY SHARTAGE FADES.

text.p: Dutch call money rates fell sharply on Tuesday, but dealers said overnight money was likely to stabilise at a level above the special advances rate soon.
Call money dropped to a bid range of 2.25-2.50 from 2.62-2.68 percent on Monday, while the advances rate is currently pegged at 2.50 percent.

Dealers said an extra advances pact on top of the regular facility had fulfilled its purpose in recent days, but was no longer needed, since the Dutch government had stopped borrowing through its short-term DTC programmes for the time being.
Earlier today, the Agency of the Ministry of Finance said it had raised another 5.67 billion guilders through its DTC programmes, ending in January, February and March.
Most of the new DTC subscriptions were likely to be settled between November 7-11, although dealers said some payments were already planned for Wednesday.
"Call money is likely to rise to the normal level, above the special advances pact," said one dealer.
The market was anticipating a substantial allocation on a new advances pact which starts running on Thursday, he added.
"DTC payments will soak up a lot of liquidity out of the market, but the central bank knows that," the dealer said.
Another dealer said the new allocation could be as great as 6.5 billion guilders. "A much smaller allocation would put upward pressure on call money rates again," he said.
The central bank was forced to offer an extra special advances pact on Friday when Thursday's allocations for a regular pact proved to be insufficient.
Dealers said they were keeping an eye out for news of the U.S. elections and Russian president Boris Yeltsin's heart operation but that these events had little effect on the market.
"No news from Russia, is good news," said one dealer, adding the market needed stability.
Dealers expected guilder-rates to stabilise in the near-term. "After that they could rise a little," said one.
Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.92 percent bid.
The guilder was a touch weaker against the mark at 112.12 from 112.11 on Monday.
